ModularUI and HEI

Use ModularUI to build a panel whose controls can read and change server data. Use HEI to show ingredients and recipes beside that panel. This guide explains how to register your panel, open it in a desktop window and close it when finished.

Opening a synchronized panel from a hosted screen keeps its last frame visible with a spinner in the top-right corner. That image is frozen: its controls do not run while the server reply is pending. The panel replaces it after attachment and layout; a failed request still shows Retry and Close. The library releases the frozen image automatically.

Choose how the screen should work

Install ModularUI on both client and server for a panel that uses server data. Install HEI on the client if you want its ingredient list, search, bookmarks and recipe pages. Neither mod is required for an ordinary local Offscreen window.

Choose an opening path
Your screen needsUseWhy
Local drawing, such as help text or a chartOffscreenAPI.open(screenFactory)No server panel is needed. Follow Your first window.
A ModularUI panel with only local controlsA client-only ModularUI screen passed to OffscreenAPI.openThe registered screen connection handles ModularUI drawing and input. This connection is called an adapter.
Slots, buttons or values backed by the serverOffscreenSimpleFactory, described belowThe server opens a matching panel and handles its data changes.

Minecraft allows one active inventory container per player. Opening another synchronized tool replaces the previous session; separate desktop windows do not give the player extra server inventories. For the same reason, opening an existing container as a local screen does not create a working server connection for it.

Register instructions for building your panel

A factory stores the instructions for building your panel. Call new OffscreenSimpleFactory(name, modId, builder) to create and register it. Keep the result for later button or key actions.

Constructor arguments
ArgumentWhat to passWhat it means
nameA unique name of at most 32 characters, such as my_addon_toolsModularUI uses this name to find the matching factory on the other side.
modIdYour actual addon ID, such as my_addonIdentifies the addon when ModularUI creates its client screen. It can differ from the factory name.
builderA function taking data, sync and settings, and returning a new ModularPanelDescribes the panel and the values or actions it shares with the server.

Register once during common initialization

Put the factory in a common class: a class available to both the client and the server. Call its registration method from your addon's common initialization handler. Both sides must use the same factory name and panel builder. Creating the factory does not open a window.

import com.cleanroommc.modularui.screen.ModularPanel;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.integration.mui2.OffscreenSimpleFactory;

public final class ModScreens {
    // Set once during common initialization. Client actions use this same factory.
    public static OffscreenSimpleFactory toolsFactory;

    private ModScreens() {}

    public static void registerScreens() {
        toolsFactory = new OffscreenSimpleFactory(
                "my_addon_tools",
                "my_addon",
                (data, sync, settings) -> {
                    // Add this panel's sync values and actions here.
                    ModularPanel panel = ModularPanel.defaultPanel("tools", 300, 200);
                    // Add your widgets to panel before returning it.
                    return panel;
                });
    }
}

Replace my_addon with your mod ID and choose a factory name your addon alone uses. Call ModScreens.registerScreens() once on each side. Repeating the constructor with an already registered name is an error. The factory stays registered for the mod's lifetime; it has no per-window close step.

ModularPanel.defaultPanel("tools", 300, 200) creates an empty panel named tools, 300 GUI units wide and 200 GUI units tall. GUI units follow Minecraft's GUI scale. They are separate from the desktop window dimensions set by OffscreenAPI.resize.

Use the three builder arguments

The builder runs when a panel is opened. The client and server each build their own copy on their game thread. Create fresh widgets and panel state inside it so one open does not reuse another open's controls. Keep Minecraft client classes, font rendering and OpenGL calls out of this common builder.

Builder inputs
InputUseful callsPurpose
GuiData datagetPlayer(), getWorld(), isClient()Find the player and world for this open, or check which side is building the panel. Plain GuiData does not include a block position.
PanelSyncManager syncsyncValue(...), registerSyncedAction(...), callSyncedAction(...)Send displayed values and control requests between the two copies.
UISettings settingscanInteractWith(...), getRecipeViewerSettings()Choose who may keep using the panel and whether its recipe viewer appears.

Declare the same sync-handler names, types and order on both sides. A handler is the piece of ModularUI code that sends or receives a value or action. Its data source may differ by side: the server reads the real value, while the client holds a copy for display. Branching on data.isClient() must not leave either copy missing a handler the other expects.

Display a server value

For a number, create an IntSyncValue and register it with sync.syncValue(name, value). Give it a server getter that reads your stored number. Give the client a place to hold the received number, then bind your display widget to that sync value.

Inputs for a displayed integer
InputWhat it does
Client getter and setterRead and update the local copy shown by the widget. Keep this copy inside the current panel's builder state.
Server getterRead the real value from your player, machine or other server-owned data.
Server setterAccept a value change on the server when your control is meant to edit it. Pass null when the sync value should not write to the stored number.
Registration nameIdentify this value within the panel, for example energy. Use the same name for the same kind of value on both sides.

The server getter supplies updates while the panel is open. Reading the client's copy is enough for drawing a label. It is not enough for deciding whether the player can spend an item or change a machine: make that decision from server data.

Send a button request to the server

Register an action with sync.registerSyncedAction(name, executeClient, executeServer, action). In the button's input callback, call sync.callSyncedAction(name). This sends a request through the panel's connection. The registered action then performs the change on the chosen side.

Action arguments
ArgumentUse for a server changeMeaning
nameA stable name such as applyConnects the button's call to its registered action.
executeClientfalseDo not perform the data change in the client's copy of the panel.
executeServertrueRun the change on the server thread.
actionA callback taking a PacketBufferRead any supplied arguments, check them, and update your server data.

For a request with no extra data, use callSyncedAction(name). To send arguments, use callSyncedAction(name, packet -> { ... }) and write the fields into the supplied buffer. Read those fields in the same order and with the same types inside the action.

Before applying a request, check that the player may use the tool and that the operation still makes sense. For example, check that the target still exists, the amount is in range and the player still owns the required items. Treat packet fields as the player's request, not proof that those conditions hold.

Use settings.canInteractWith(player -> ...) for a rule that must remain true while the panel is open. ModularUI checks this rule each tick and closes the UI when it returns false. The action still needs its own checks because the data may have changed since the previous tick.

Open the panel from client input

Once registration has finished, call ModScreens.toolsFactory.openOffscreen() from a client button or key handler. A world and player must already be available. Keep its return value in the client controller that owns this tool.

import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.OffscreenAPI;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.window.Window;

// Fields and methods inside your client controller.
private Window toolsWindow;

void openTools() {
    if (OffscreenAPI.isOpen(toolsWindow)) return;
    toolsWindow = ModScreens.toolsFactory.openOffscreen();
    if (OffscreenAPI.isOpen(toolsWindow)) {
        OffscreenAPI.setTitle(toolsWindow, "Tools");
    }
}

The guard keeps repeated clicks from replacing this controller's live window. Keep the client controller out of common startup code so a dedicated server never loads its window or GUI classes.

Opening options and results
Call or resultMeaning
openOffscreen()Open with the operating system's normal title bar.
openOffscreen(chrome)Use a WindowChrome configuration at creation. See window appearance for its options.
nullNo player or world is available, a different factory is waiting to open, or a usable window could not be kept.
An exceptionSetup failed. Native window creation errors can throw; inspect the cause before retrying.

Wait for the panel to be ready

The native window opens before the server replies, so it first shows Waiting for server…. OffscreenAPI.isOpen(toolsWindow) reports that the window exists. OffscreenAPI.isReady(toolsWindow) reports that the server's panel is installed and its first layout is complete. Both calls accept null.

Return from the input handler after opening. Check readiness from a later client update if you need the panel's layout; do not block the client thread waiting for it, because that thread must also process the reply.

While a request is waiting, reopening that factory returns its existing waiting window. A request for another factory returns null. If no usable reply arrives within roughly 200 client maintenance ticks, the connection is released and the window offers Retry and Close. A timeout is not a count of rendered frames. See opening failures if it keeps happening.

Kotlin, Scala and Groovy can call these Java methods directly. ZenScript can request a factory by name with Windows.openSynchronized("my_addon_tools"). It returns a script window handle, whose ready property reports readiness and whose close() method ends the session.

Close the tool and its session

Call this method from the tool's close action and your client disconnect or unload hook:

void closeTools() {
    OffscreenAPI.close(toolsWindow);
    toolsWindow = null;
}

close accepts a null or already closed handle. For an open synchronized window, it ends the server session, removes its network connection and releases the native window resources. If the server closes the panel, Offscreen also ends that session. Leave request IDs and late replies to the factory; it keeps an old reply from attaching to a newer window.

The factory does not save your panel's data to disk. Store lasting values in your addon's normal saved data. Cancel background work and remove any listeners your own code created when their screen or controller is disposed; closing the window cannot release unrelated resources your addon kept elsewhere.

Choose whether HEI is shown

Offscreen connects HEI to supported container screens automatically when HEI is installed. For ModularUI panels, use settings.getRecipeViewerSettings() inside the panel builder to choose the overlay behavior:

Recipe-viewer settings
CallResult
settings.getRecipeViewerSettings().defaultState()Use ModularUI's default: enable the recipe viewer for synchronized GUIs and leave it disabled for client-only GUIs.
settings.getRecipeViewerSettings().enable()Request the overlay, including for a client-only GUI. HEI must still be installed and support the screen.
settings.getRecipeViewerSettings().disable()Hide the recipe viewer for this panel.

Leaving these settings untouched uses defaultState. Calling them is safe when no recipe viewer is installed; they do not install HEI or add its ingredient data themselves.

Keep the overlay clear of your controls

If a widget sits outside the panel, add it as an exclusion area so HEI tries to place its overlay around it. Call settings.getRecipeViewerSettings().addExclusionArea(widget) with that widget. You can also pass a java.awt.Rectangle for a fixed screen area.

Exclusion-area arguments
ArgumentUseRemoval
A ModularUI widgetReserve the area occupied by a control, especially one outside its parent panel.Pass the same widget to removeExclusionArea(widget) if it should stop reserving space while the panel is still open.
new Rectangle(x, y, width, height)Reserve a fixed rectangle in screen GUI coordinates.Keep the rectangle object and pass that same instance to removeExclusionArea(area).

Each desktop window has its own overlay layout, search widget and recipe-page history. Ingredient data and bookmarks remain shared. Offscreen removes its window's search listeners when the window closes, without removing listeners belonging to another window.

This integration targets ModularUI 3.1.6 and HEI 4.36.1. HEI support does not make every arbitrary GuiScreen an ingredient-aware container screen.
